study_title: Self-Determination Theory (SDT) in Financial Dependence Policies
description: Data collection schema for evaluating how specific financial support policies impact a person's autonomy, competence, and relatedness.

policy_context.conditions: Must perform 15 hours of household chores/week

autonomy.qualitative_notes: Participant feels in control of their daily schedule despite receiving financial support, as the arrangement was explicitly agreed upon.

competence.qualitative_notes: The requirement to contribute labor in exchange for the allowance creates a sense of capability and purpose.

relatedness.qualitative_notes: Participant feels highly connected and valued; reciprocity prevents the guilt usually associated with over-benefiting.

policy_context.conditions: Must ask for funds for personal items

autonomy.qualitative_notes: Feels financially at their partner's mercy; lack of direct access to joint accounts severely limits freedom.

competence.qualitative_notes: Feels capable as a parent, but feels financially incompetent due to lack of earning power.

relatedness.qualitative_notes: The visible and conditional nature of the financial support creates resentment and isolates the participant.
